problem.text: Let $a$, $b$, $c$, and $d$ be positive integers such that $\gcd(a,b)=24$, $\gcd(b,c)=36$, $\gcd(c,d)=54$, and $70<\gcd(d,a)<100$. Which of the following must be a divisor of $a$?

steps.title: Where to start: look at powers of $2$ and $3$
steps.body:
All three given gcds are built only from $2$s and $3$s:
$$24=2^3\cdot3,\quad 36=2^2\cdot3^2,\quad 54=2\cdot3^3.$$
A gcd takes the smaller power of each prime from the two numbers. So track exactly how many $2$s and $3$s each of $a,b,c,d$ has; that will pin down part of $\gcd(d,a)$.

your_turn.prompt: From $\gcd(a,b)=24$ and $\gcd(b,c)=36$, what is the least power of $3$ that $b$ must have? And the least power of $2$?
your_turn.answer: $b$ has at least $3^2$ (from $36$) and at least $2^3$ (from $24$).

steps.title: Find the exact powers in $a$, $c$, and $d$
steps.body: $b$ has at least $3^2$, but $\gcd(a,b)$ has only $3^1$, so the smaller power must come from $a$: $a$ has exactly one $3$. In the same way, $b$ has at least $2^3$ but $\gcd(b,c)$ has only $2^2$, so $c$ has exactly $2^2$.

your_turn.prompt: Now use $\gcd(c,d)=54=2\cdot3^3$. How many $2$s does $d$ have exactly?
your_turn.answer: Exactly one: $c$ has $2^2$, but the gcd has only $2^1$, so the smaller power $2^1$ comes from $d$.

steps.title: What $\gcd(d,a)$ looks like
steps.body: Also $a$ has at least $2^3$ (from $24$) and $d$ has at least $3^3$ (from $54$). So in $\gcd(d,a)$ the power of $2$ is $\min(1,\text{at least }3)=1$ and the power of $3$ is $\min(\text{at least }3,1)=1$. That means $\gcd(d,a)=6k$, where $k$ is not divisible by $2$ or $3$. Careful: "a multiple of $6$" is not enough; $k$ may not add any more $2$s or $3$s.

your_turn.prompt: List the multiples of $6$ strictly between $70$ and $100$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Of $k=12,13,14,15,16$, the numbers $12,14,16$ are even and $15$ is a multiple of $3$. Only $k=13$ works, so $\gcd(d,a)=78=2\cdot3\cdot13$ and $13$ divides $a$. For example, $a=312$, $b=72$, $c=108$, $d=702$ fits every condition, and $312$ is not divisible by $5$, $7$, $11$ or $17$. The answer is **(D)**.

wrong_choices.A: This comes from taking $\gcd(d,a)=90$ because it is a multiple of $6$. But $90=2\cdot3^2\cdot5$ has two $3$s, and $a$ has only one.
wrong_choices.B: This comes from taking $\gcd(d,a)=84$ because it is a multiple of $6$. But $84=2^2\cdot3\cdot7$ has two $2$s, and $d$ has only one.
